purpose: Test whether the final demonstration labels contribute to unique-candidate replacement bias, keeping all ten demonstration pairs and every rule/candidate/source/context/schema unchanged.
comparisonScope: If preregistered after current study closure, compare entire101-source arms, never only failing cases. Preserve supported ASR repair requirements and all literal/meaning boundaries; no acceptance threshold relaxation or semantic output rejection.
limits: Ordering is a hypothesis, not established causality. Existing current last three examples are positive; future terminal-negative ordering may trade harmful corrections for missed repairs and must be rejected if it does so.
priorEvidence: Round61 appended four novel demonstrations after original ten. Their labels are keep, mixed replace/keep, keep, replace; the last is still positive. It reduced overall conformance. It did not isolate unchanged-pair ordering or terminal-negative ordering; no recency explanation is established.
